issues.description: Constructors of Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat: the solution repository defines constructors that accept (String name, int age) (e.g., Animal(String name, int age) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java and corresponding two-parameter constructors in Seal, Pig, Goat). The problem statement UML and the provided template Main use single-argument constructors that accept only the name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle") in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java and the UML shows only a name attribute for Animal). This mismatch prevents the example Main from compiling against the solution code and confuses students which constructor signature they must implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent across all artifacts. Option A (preferred for minimal problem change): remove the age parameter from the solution's Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat constructors and the age field from Animal so each concrete animal has a single-argument constructor (String name) that matches the UML and the template Main. Option B: If age is desired, update the problem statement/UML and the template Main to declare and demonstrate constructors that accept (String name, int age) and document the new 'age' attribute accordingly. Apply the chosen option to template code, problem text, and solution so all artifacts match.

issues.description: Animal.age attribute: the solution's class de.tum.cit.ase.Animal declares a private int age field (line declaring 'private int age;') which is not present in the UML or described in the problem statement (the UML/description specify only a name attribute for Animal). This additional attribute introduces an implementation requirement not described in the exercise and contributes to constructor signature divergence.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the 'age' field (and its getters/setters/constructor parameter) from the solution's Animal class so the class only contains the 'name' attribute as specified in the UML/problem statement, or update the UML/problem statement and template to explicitly include 'age' as an attribute of Animal and require it in constructors and documentation. Ensure all artifacts consistently document and implement the same attributes.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and concrete animal classes: The problem statement and UML describe animals having a name and ask for constructors that initialize class attributes (implying a single-argument constructor for name). The template Main instantiates animals using a single String argument (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). However, the solution's Animal class declares a constructor public Animal(String name, int age) and the concrete classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) declare matching two-parameter constructors (String name, int age) and add an 'age' attribute. Students following the problem text or template Main will expect constructors like Seal(String), Pig(String), Goat(String), so the solution API (with an additional 'age' parameter and attribute) will be unexpected and can cause compilation errors or confusion when mapping requirements to code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor API across artifacts. Choose one of the following consistent remedies: (A) Remove the 'age' attribute from Animal and change solution constructors to single-argument forms (Animal(String name); Seal(String name); Pig(String name); Goat(String name)) to match the UML/problem and template Main. (B) Update the problem statement and template Main to require and demonstrate two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", 3)) and document the 'age' attribute in the UML and description. (C, minimal disruption) Add overloaded single-argument constructors in the solution that delegate to the two-argument constructors with a default age (e.g., public Seal(String name) { this(name, 0); }) so the template Main examples compile while preserving the age attribute.
